title: How can you realistically trust beta testers that aren't people you know?
author: No_Departure7494
selftext: Working on a game now and would love to get some people to play it but with AI there's almost a comedic irony in knowing they could get Claude to make their own little rendition of your creation.

comments.author: because-potato
comments.body:
You can’t - test it yourself and with family members/friends only. 

If it’s for the Google play console beta testing, register as an organization account to bypass the restriction.

replies.author: Creepy-Doughnut-5054
replies.body: you are acting like making org acc is something you can do in 1 minute.

replies.author: because-potato
replies.body: Took me literally 2 days… what’s the rush?

replies.author: Trick_Mention_8687
replies.body: Whoa what? I assume you already had a company registration or something?

replies.author: because-potato
replies.body: No. Registered my LLC on a Sunday, paperwork approved Monday night, called and got my DUNS on a Tuesday, and Google play approved my DUNS that night. Spent $75 all in.

comments.author: BratPit24
comments.body:
I mean. This is the modern day. You either make them sign super aggressive NDA. Or live with the danger.

Can't love the pork without dealing with pig shit.

comments.author: zit-hb
comments.body: Such is life. At least, you have a head start. Unless your beta goes viral there is a low likelihood of it happening though. Getting beta testers that you don't know alone is already a challenge... People drown in choice.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
I said it in another thread and it's worth saying here:

People clone successful things. Nobody's going to clone your game if it's not yet proven any success.

replies.author: Brewgazer
replies.body: Yup and if they clone it they probably won’t look at every detail the way the person with the original idea will so if anything feel flattered someone thought your game was gonna go big

comments.author: Original_Hat_42
comments.body:
I \*only\* trust strangers to test my game. I value the anonymity, their lack of reason to do me any favors, the genuine nature of their engagement.

Then again, I don't really worry they can steal my game. It's not a concept game where the first one to get it out there wins. It's a deep puzzle game. They'd never be able to reconstruct the state engine. The presentation is trash. It's possible that doesn't apply to your game.

comments.author: ipreuss
comments.body:
Unless your game is trivial, any copy will probably have areas where it will be worse than your original. 

It might also have areas where it’s better, or new ideas that work really well. Then you just copy those back. 🤷‍♂️

comments.author: LootavaGames
comments.body:
I’m actually dealing with this right now. I’m developing a mobile game solo and just opened closed alpha testing to people I don’t know.  
Sure, someone could copy the idea, but I’m much more worried about building something nobody wants to play. I’d rather get honest feedback early than keep everything hidden.

comments.author: MessageSelfdestructs
comments.body:
Fuck me - are you all so deluded you're creating the next Minecraft?

How about you actually create your fuckin game in the first place, and then we can talk if it's actually worth duping (probably not...).

replies.author: No_Departure7494
replies.body: Tough guy, practice some civility. Every one else managed to respond in a normal manner but you.

comments.author: TalkingHeadsVideo
comments.body: Decades ago, I had a friend making a dice game based on a regional table game.  The problem is he became obsessed with protecting his product(a game he is copying, keep in mind), and he started spending more time writing code to prevent piracy than on the actual game. Eventually, he was able to prevent people from pirating it by never releasing it.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: Obfuscate your code if you're worried, before you push any builds to strangers. Better yet, do that and give them a specific testing build that only has whatever it is you're trying to test. You don't need to have it packing in the entire game. Make it like the demo version where it's a slice. If it's something like a metroidvania you'd only have a slice with the first required abilities in the code. If it was a Survivors type game you'd have a couple upgrade options and maybe a level. If it's a survival RPG you'd have a few of the blueprints, resources and mechanics and maybe one biome. Etc.

comments.author: ArcyRC
comments.body:
They can steal your ideas.

They can't steal your brain. 

GO FORTH AND CREATE MORE

comments.author: Brettinabox
comments.body: An idea is not the same as execution.
